MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 10, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on October 10, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 5, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Initiation of Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (4)
  of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - 2 Cases.

CS2. Threat to Public Services or Facilities. Consultation with City of Mission Viejo Cyber
  Security/Video Operations Manager; City Attorney.

City Council Minutes  1  October 10, 2017
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Mayor Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PRESENTATIONS

Items P1 and P2 were taken out of order.

P2.  20th Anniversary of the Mission Viejo Library

  Robert Breton presented a pictorial history of the Mission Viejo Library and Mayor
  Bucknum presented a proclamation to Genesis Hansen, Director of Library Services.

P1.  Proclaim October 8 through 14, 2017 To Be "Fire Prevention Week"

  Mayor Bucknum made the presentation to Mayor Pro Tem Sachs who accepted the
  proclamation as Vice Chair of the Orange County Fire Authority Board of Directors.

P3.  2017 Walk Against Drugs

  Crime Prevention Specialist Khatra Molina discussed the 29th Annual Walk Against Drugs
  and South County Disaster Preparedness Expo which will be held on Saturday, October
  21, 2017.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Doug Zielasko, Chief Operating Officer of the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce, M.V.:
announced that the Chamber of Commerce is hosting a State of the City event on November 11,
2017, from 6:00 to 9:00 p.m. at Arroyo Trabuco Golf Club. Tickets are now available at
citygala.missionviejochamber.com.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: expressed her dissatisfaction with the Chamber’s State of the City event and
she noted that it has been tradition, for 30 years, to show a State of the City video at a City Council
Meeting instead.

Margot Ferron, Rancho Santa Margarita: invited the community to a night of comedy on Friday,
October 27, 2017, at 7:30 p.m. at the Murray Community Center. The comedy show is a fundraiser
for the town of Port Aransas, Texas, which was heavily damaged during Hurricane Harvey.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: shared her concerns with the condition of City slopes and discussed a lawsuit
that was filed against the City after a slope failure. She also said that there is an ongoing issue with
trees blocking the line of sight to a traffic signal on Muirlands at Marathon.
City Council Minutes  2  October 10, 2017
 Ryan Farsai, M.V.: stated that the City illegally placed an LCD sign on his property and does not
have a grant deed or quit claim deed.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of September 26, 2017, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated September 15, 2017 in the Amount of $2,551,018.88

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated September 22, 2017 in the Amount of $766,512.81

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Amending the City of Mission Viejo Salary Schedule and Authorized Position
  Schedule

  Adopted Resolution 17-45 Amending the City’s Salary Schedule and Authorized Position
  Schedule Effective October 11, 2017.

5.  Year-End Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo for the Twelve Months
  Ended June 30, 2017

  Received and filed.

6.  Semi-Annual Financial Report for the Community Development Financing Authority
  for the Year Ended June 30, 2017

  Received and filed.

7.  Purchase of Pool Chemicals for Public Swimming Pools and Spas at City of Mission
  Viejo Recreation Centers

City Council Minutes  3  October 10, 2017
   (1) Awarded a contract to Waterline Technologies for the period of November 1, 2017, to
  June 30, 2019, in the amount of $251,744.40; and (2) issued a purchase order for the period
  of November 1, 2017, to June 30, 2018, in an amount not to exceed $88,405.20 for the
  purchase of pool chemicals for public swimming pools and spas at City of Mission Viejo
  Recreation Centers.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

8.  2017 Citywide Speed Limit Update

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented a brief staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Ordinance 17-326 Amending Chapter 12.04.010(d) of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code
  Regarding Prima Facie Speed Limits on Certain Streets.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

9.  CalPERS Annual Valuation Report dated June 30, 2016

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to direct
  staff to not make any additional contributions over and above the City's annual payment.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

10.  Close out of FY 2016/17 and FY 2017/18 Budget Adjustments for Certain Revenue
  and Expenditure Accounts

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report and Director of
  Information Technology Jackie Alexander answered the City Council Member’s questions
  relative to the replacement of staff computers.

City Council Minutes  4  October 10, 2017
   Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to (1) adopted
  Resolution 17-46 Amending the FY 2016/17 City Budget for Year-End Close Out
  Adjustments in Certain Accounts and Funds; (2) adopt Resolution 17-47 Amending the
  FY 2017/18 City Budget.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  By consensus, the City Council directed staff to put the remaining funds in to the reserves
  as outlined in the staff report and return with a recommendation for purchasing new staff
  computers and identifying possible funding sources.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

11.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report during item P1.

12.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Mayor Bucknum presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

13.  Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) Update

  Lt. Ken Binning discussed the Sheriff Department’s response to loud party calls over the
  summer and he noted that the City’s ordinance for multiple responses to loud parties and
  the social host ordinance are working. He also responded to previous public comments on
  lack of enforcement at Cordova Park and he demonstrated that the Sheriff’s Department
  has done quite a bit of patrolling, enforcement and citation work at the park in recent
  months. Lt. Binning responded to Council questions about an alleged fraudulent jewelry
  store owner and how the Sheriff’s Department might help bring some resolve to residents
  who have judgments against the store owner.

Update on the Marguerite Aquatics Complex Renovation Project

Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented a pictorial update on
the renovation project at the Aquatics Center.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

14.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

City Council Minutes  5  October 10, 2017
   By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell mentioned that he had to spring into action yesterday to take care of his
niece who lives in Tustin Ranch and was being evacuated due to the nearby fire. He said the
impact of that evacuation scene was very emotional for him and his niece and he hopes that
everyone is ready with a plan. Council Member Goodell noted that Orange County can be a
dangerous place during fire season and seeing that firsthand really brought it home for him.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she was pleased to attend the opioid crisis presentation at
San Juan Hills High School on October 2. She said it was a very informational two-hour session
on the drug crisis that has impacted our communities and the presentation is now available online.
Council Member Kelley stated that it has been a really rough couple of weeks for the country and
she has been very interested to read the stories of people who helped save lives in the midst of the
chaos in the Las Vegas tragedy. She learned that one of the life savers, Jimmy Grovom, graduated
from Capistrano Valley High School in 2010. He was at the concert, saw people getting shot, and
immediately jumped into action. After his brother and girlfriend got to safety Mr. Grovom was
tending to a gunshot victim when he too was shot in the leg. Council Member Kelley noted that he
put the welfare and safety of others above his own and there were also five law enforcement
personnel from the Orange County Sheriff’s Department on vacation when disaster struck, and
they too jumped into action. Council Member Kelley imparted a special thank you to the thousands
of firefighters, up and down the state, including Orange County Fire Authority firefighters who
are battling the many blazes. In closing, she announced that the Community of Character word for
the month of October is respect.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths stated that he is personally very honored to serve on the City Council and
to be a part of the City. He said he was walking around the Murray Community Center the other
day and he saw seniors playing bocce ball, kids playing soccer, and more residents doing activities
inside the center. He recalled that when there was an issue with Cordova Park and a neighborhood
that needed extra attention, the Sheriff’s Department and City Code personnel took care of keeping
an eye on the community. Council Member Raths asked staff to provide him with some additional
information about the property issue with the Arco station and Mr. Ryan Farsai.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs talked about the Marine who stole a pickup truck to transport injured people
to the hospital after the Las Vegas shooting and said that he thought it was great that a car dealer
just gifted the Marine a new truck. Discussing pension liability, Mayor Pro Tem Sachs reported
that a Nobel Prize winner from Stanford University has recently finished a study on the California
Pension System and he looked at five counties and five cities to evaluate their pension issues.
City Council Minutes  6  October 10, 2017
 Mayor Pro Tem Sachs cited some of the conclusions of the study noting that while pension funding
amounts have increased, governments have reduced social, welfare and educational services as
well as softer services including libraries, recreation and community services. He stated these are
some of the things the Council is trying to prevent in Mission Viejo and he distributed a listing
that he made of the City’s unfunded liability amounts with the assumption of a 5% yearly increase.
He reviewed the numbers and pointed out that by the year 2024 the City’s unfunded liability, based
on the estimated growth, would be close to half of the City’s general fund.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum reminded residents that the Mission Viejo Library’s 20th anniversary celebration
will be held on Saturday, October 14, 2017, beginning at 10:00 a.m. She said there will be
something for everyone and the event will culminate with a concert at the end of the day. She
discussed her attendance at other anniversary celebrations including Capistrano Valley High
School’s 40th anniversary alumni parade and Mount of Olives 50th anniversary Oktoberfest. Mount
of Olives will also host an event called “Miracle on the 405” on Sunday, October 15 where people
who survived the recent plane crash on the freeway will talk about that experience. Mayor
Bucknum discussed her participation in the walk to school day with Bathgate Elementary students
and her attendance at a forum for adults on bigotry, bullying and bravery. Parents learned what
they can do to help kids and she noted that bullying has taken on a whole new nuance with cell
phones and social media. Mayor Bucknum announced that the Chamber of Commerce is trying to
elevate the organization and they came to the City with a series of ideas for new events this year.
In addition to Restaurant Week, they proposed to host a State of the City event, doing something
more formal, festive and fun for their members. Mayor Bucknum provided a reminder that the City
has committed to Economic Development efforts and to making the economy in Mission Viejo
more business friendly. She said that every Council Member has that goal and the City needs to
have a different relationship and partnership with the Chamber going forward. The State of the
City event, which is on Veterans Day, will honor vets, highlight women in leadership and will be
a great opportunity for the Chamber to raise money so she encouraged people to support that effort.
Mayor Bucknum talked about the Mission Viejo residents that were touched by the situation in
Las Vegas and reported that Mission Viejo resident and gunshot victim Matt Cox is now home
from Las Vegas and recovering. In closing, she discussed the Mission for Armed Forces event and
read a thank you letter from Sergeant Robert Massey, a veteran, who wished to thank the City and
Coach Johnson for putting on such a great tribute and honoring him for serving his country.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:41 p.m., with no further business to come before the Council at this session, Mayor
Bucknum adjourned the meeting in memory of those that perished in Las Vegas, to Tuesday,
October 24, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

____________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 24, 2017

City Council Minutes  7  October 10, 2017
